source.description: StreetLight Data select-link analysis of Hillegass Ave and Colby St between Alcatraz Ave and Claremont Ave, January–July 2025, provided by residents.
source.throughNote: wholeStreetVehPerHour and endAlongVehPerHour are DATA from the resident volunteer count of 2025-02-25 (data/calibration/rockridge.volunteer-count-2025-02-25.json, routeDiagrams tableTotals: cars that drove the whole street, cars whose trip ended along it). The calibrate report turns them into an observed through range: whole-street cars up to block volume less end-along cars.
source.caveat: Sample does not represent all travelers. Shares are of trips traversing the analyzed segment, each direction analyzed separately.

freewayRamp.sideNote: The shares are for traffic coming from (on-ramp) or going to (off-ramp) the north of the ramps; a via street with "north of X" counts only its links north of X.

ontoFreewayFromNorth.via: Telegraph Avenue north of Alcatraz Avenue

acceptance.note: Thresholds of design decisions D16 to D18 (openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-13-baseline-calibration/design.md). Stability is judged over the fixed seed list below on seed means and seed shares; the old rule (zero removals in every seed, backlog under 2%, arterial speed above 4 m/s) is kept in the reports for comparison.

patterns.note: Diagnostics of reported behavior, read by the calibrate report. They have no observed counterpart in the StreetLight figures; the related observed shares are the select-link rows (College Avenue 6% northbound from Hillegass Avenue, 21 to 33% to Benvenue Avenue).

freewayThrough.description: Trips between the surface gates north of the ramps and the freeway mainline gates, and the local-street vehicle-miles they drive.

qualitative: A resident reports that Hillegass Avenue and Colby Street carry clearly more than about 100 vehicles an hour at the PM peak, that many drivers from Berkeley cut through to Highway 24, and that Hillegass Avenue is used as a bypass for College Avenue. This is an observation, not a count; the volumes implied by the ramp counts and the observed shares are in the demand fit report.
Little drop-off in freeway-bound and freeway-origin traffic between Claremont Avenue and Alcatraz Avenue: these trips continue through the neighborhood.
Southbound freeway-bound drivers on College Avenue commonly arrive via Ashby Avenue and Benvenue Avenue, then jog to Hillegass Avenue.
Traffic on Martin Street and Colby Street is largely traveling between the freeway and Telegraph Avenue.

travelTimes.note: DATA: average travel speed (mph) over arterial segments in the weekday peak periods, from the Alameda CTC level-of-service monitoring: floating-car runs (6 or 7 per segment) or commercial probe speeds, count years 2012 and 2014 [ACTC-LOS2014], 2016 and 2018 [ACTC-LOS2018]. The assessment compares the simulated time over the same segment (free-flow time plus mean link delay, seed mean) with the range of the four years. A target for reading, not a fit constraint.

intentMap._note: Round 21. What the resident volunteer count of Feb 25, 2025 and the headline freeway shares imply about the intent of through cars (where they came from and where they were going) on the four counted blocks, PM peak. `from` and `to` are approach groups or sets of the area config. Implied veh/h are inferred from the counts with the stated ASSUMPTION shares; `low` and `high` bound them. Nothing here is a count of origins and destinations: no source gives those.
intentMap.note: Through = neither trip end is in the study area. Groups are the approach groups of the area config (data/areas); a node that is not a gate takes the group of the nearest surface gate (ASSUMPTION). The arterial is the one a trip would use on the shortest free-flow path with the study area's residential and service streets closed, where that path runs on a boundary street near the study area.

blocks.note: Observed (PM): 182 cars entered at the south end, 102 drove the whole street, 164 left it at Alcatraz Ave (131 left, 32 right, 1 straight), and 47% of the block's trips came from a freeway (the headline share). ASSUMPTION: freeway-origin cars that do not end along the street are 65 veh/h (the 82 freeway-origin trips on the block, 47% of 174, times the 182 / (182 + 47) of its cars that entered at the south end rather than joining on the way), spread over the 164 exits in proportion (0.40); the other through cars come from the Telegraph Ave and south-side approaches that feed the street's south end. Ranges: low = 131 (32) x 0.47 x 0.62 (the whole-street share of exits), high = 131 (32) x 0.47.
